messages:
elaine: @matt @raj heads-up — Fjord Labs (dedicated pool fjord-prod) is seeing intermittent tail-latency regressions after the kernel-selector changes yesterday. p95 jumped from ~210ms to ~420ms during busy windows. KV cache hit rate dropped from ~72% -> 38% on their workload. suspect continuous-batcher is forming many tiny batches and token-bucket refill is starving batching windows. attaching quick profile + proposed per-customer smoothing.

matt: can you paste the profile and current batch/queue config? also what model variant are they on? :eyes:

elaine: model: redwood-open-13b-q4. kernel-selector v2.4.1 rolled at 03:10 UTC. sample profile (10:30–10:45):
```
PROFILING SUMMARY
window: 900s
requests: 18k
avg tokens/request: 78
KV cache hit: 38%
avg batch size (seq tokens): 3.2
p50/p95/p99 lat ms: 128 / 420 / 980
hotspot: kernel_selector::select_kernel (stalls on shape mismatch) ~22% CPU
continuous-batcher: emit-rate high, many 1-2 request microbatches
```

elaine: current dedicated config for fjord-prod (excerpt):
```
batching:
  max_window_ms: 14
  max_tokens_per_batch: 8192
  min_batch_tokens: 64
queue_policy:
  queue_size: 2048
  token_bucket_rate: 4000 # tokens/sec
  token_bucket_burst: 8000
per_customer_overrides: {}
```

raj: hmm, kernel-selector change may have tightened kernel matching which increases fallback paths and small batch performance hit. two levers that seem low-risk: 1) increase continuous-batcher window slightly to let batches coalesce, 2) apply per-customer token_bucket smoothing so burst isn't consumed by short requests. propose token_bucket_rate -> 2200 and burst -> 12000, and bump max_window_ms -> 26 for fjord-prod only. that should raise avg batch tokens -> ~7.

sophie: + consider KV prefetch tuning too — their workload has long prefixes so cache warm is crucial. we can enable async kv-prefetch for fjord-prod: admit prefetch for first 16 tokens of common prefixes, ttl 60s.

matt: agree with raj. also add a quick canary: change for 10% of fjord capacity, monitor p95, kv hit. if regression persists, rollback kernel-selector for that pool or route them to quantized-8 model fallback.

elaine: draft per-customer override to push:
```
per_customer_overrides:
  fjord-prod:
    batching:
      max_window_ms: 26
      min_batch_tokens: 128
    queue_policy:
      token_bucket_rate: 2200
      token_bucket_burst: 12000
    kv_prefetch:
      enabled: true
      prefix_tokens: 16
      ttl_s: 60
    canary_percent: 10
```

matt: looks good. add a metric watchlist: fjord.p95, fjord.kv_hit, fjord.avg_batch_tokens, fjord.queue_depth. alert if p95 > 350ms or kv_hit < 55% for 5m.

elaine: will push as a config patch to config-store + create rollout PR. plan: canary for 2h, watch metrics, then ramp to 100% over 30m if green. tagging @deploy-bot to schedule canary window.

deploy-bot: deploy scheduled: config-store:update/1945012345-fjord-smoothing-canary -> canary start 2026-03-18T15:10:00Z (10% capacity) ; auto-check at +2h; rollback if alert triggered.

raj: one more note — kernel-selector team, we should instrument kernel selection path to emit fallback-count per request (small extra metric) so we can correlate later. pinging in a follow-up.

sophie: i'll draft the KV prefetch toggle as a feature-flag so we can flip quickly.

elaine: thanks all. I'll attach the PR and the quick grafana dashboard links once created. :+1:
